{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Terrie Christine Stevens''', also known as '''T. Christine Stevens''', is an American mathematician whose research concerns [[topological group]]s, the [[history of mathematics]], and [[mathematics education]].<ref name="profile">[http://www.siam.org/visiting/speakers/stevens.php Speaker bio], [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], retrieved 2015-01-25.</ref> She is also known as the co-founder of [[Project NExT]], a mentorship program for recent doctorates in mathematics, which she directed from 1994 until 2009.<ref name="next">[http://www.maa.org/programs/faculty-and-departments/project-next Project NExt], [[Mathematical Association of America]], retrieved 2015-01-25.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=AMS Sponsors NExT Fellows|department=Inside the AMS|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=56|issue=10|page=1310|first=Aparna|last=Higgins|author-link=Aparna Higgins|date=November 2009|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200910/rtx091001310p.pdf}}.</ref><ref name="scm">{{citation|title=MAA Member Chris Stevens Awarded Smith College Medal|date=September 17, 2009|journal=MAA News|department=Math in the News|url=http://www.maa.org/news/math-news/maa-member-chris-stevens-awarded-smith-college-medal|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Stevens graduated from [[Smith College]] in 1970,<ref name="smith">[http://www.smith.edu/newsoffice/releases/NewsOffice09-044.html Smith College Rally Day: Honors, Hats and a Secret Revealed], [[Smith College]], September 10, 2009, retrieved 2015-01-25.</ref> and completed her doctorate in 1978 at [[Harvard University]] under the supervision of [[Andrew M. Gleason]]. Her dissertation was ''Weakened Topologies for Lie Groups''.<ref name="jackson"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=69662}}</ref>

She held teaching positions at the [[University of Massachusetts Lowell]], at [[Mount Holyoke College]] and at [[Arkansas State University]] before joining [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]], where for 25 years she was a professor of mathematics and computer science.<ref name="berry"/><ref name="jackson"/>

She was also a Congressional Science Fellow assisting congressman [[Theodore S. Weiss]] in 1984–1985,<ref name="profile"/><ref name="smith"/> and was a program officer at the [[National Science Foundation]] in 1987–1989.<ref name="profile"/> After retiring from SLU, she became Associate Executive Director for Meetings and Professional Services of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref name="hay"/><ref name="jackson">{{citation|title=Chris Stevens Joins AMS Executive Staff|journal=Notices of the AMS|first=Allyn|last=Jackson|volume=62|issue=1|pages=56–57|date=January 2015|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201501/rnoti-p56.pdf|doi=10.1090/noti1201|doi-access=free}}.</ref> She also served as an [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]] Council member at large from 2011 to 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1997 Stevens received the [[Deborah and Franklin Haimo Awards for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics|Deborah and Franklin Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics]].<ref name=web>{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award|title=Recipients of the Deborah and Franklin Tepper Haimo Award for Distinguished College or University Teaching of Mathematics; Mathematical Association of America|website=www.maa.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240608175318/https://maa.org/member-communities/maa-awards/teaching-awards/section-award |archive-date=8 June 2024 }}</ref>

In 2004 she won the Gung and Hu Award for
Distinguished Service to Mathematics of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] for her work on Project NExT.<ref name="jackson"/><ref name="berry">{{citation|title=Professor Earns Highest Honor from Leading Mathematics Organization|publisher=[[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis University]]|first=Clayton|last=Berry|date=January 28, 2004|url=http://www.slu.edu/readstory/more/3752|accessdate=2015-01-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215905/http://www.slu.edu/readstory/more/3752|archive-date=March 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

In 2010 she was awarded the Smith College Medal by her alma mater.<ref name="scm"/><ref name="smith"/>

She has been a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] since 2005,<ref>[https://www.aaas.org/elected-fellows Elected Fellows], AAAS, retrieved 2017-10-30.</ref>
and in 2012, she became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2015-01-25.</ref>

She was the 2015 winner of the [[Louise Hay Award]] of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]].<ref name="hay">[https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/announcements/2015awmlouisehayaward 2015 AWM Louise Hay Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161008184819/https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/home/announcements/2015awmlouisehayaward |date=2016-10-08 }}, [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], retrieved 2015-01-25.</ref>
